programs.title: Crime in Post-War Germany
programs.desc: Germany, 1945. A nation faces up to the ruins of its past. Hunger and adversity shape daily life. What lengths did people go to? Over two episodes, Crime in Post-War Germany explores this transitional phase in German history by using the examples of individual, particularly serious criminal cases. Criminal psychologists and forensics experts go in search of traces.

programs.title: The D-Days Spies
programs.desc: Discover how agents tricked the Germans to keep their troops out of Normandy.

programs.title: The Soldier who never was
programs.desc: Discover a darkly humorous British ploy that helped the 1943 landing in Sicily.

programs.title: The Spy who Saved the World
programs.desc: Discover how a Soviet Intelligence officer avoided WWIII.

programs.title: The A-Bomb Spies
programs.desc: Discover how and why several brilliant scientists divulged the secrets of the atomic bomb.

programs.title: The Rise of Judea
programs.desc: The Rise of Judea explores the tumultuous reign of King Herod and the ascent of Roman stewardship in Judea through the words of Flavius Josephus.

programs.title: The Fall of Judea
programs.desc: The Fatal Conflict Episode 2 explores the events that shaped the great Jewish revolt against Rome, as recorded by Jewish General, historian and perceived traitor, Flavius Josephus.

programs.title: Birth of a Brotherhood
programs.desc: At the beginning of the 12th century, a few knights decide to create a new brotherhood called "The order of the Temple".

programs.title: A business empire
programs.desc: In the middle of the 12th century, the order of the Temple becomes increasingly popular among the kings and peoples of Western Europe.

programs.title: The fall of the order
programs.desc: At the end of the 13th century, as Christian holdings in the holy land have disappeared, the Templars continue to push for a new crusade.

programs.title: In the Footsteps of Jesus
programs.desc: For the past 2000 years, he has remained the most famous character of History. Described as a leader, as a feminist, an anarchist, a healer. But today, what do we really know about Jesus?

programs.title: The Miracles of Jesus
programs.desc: For more than 2000 years, he has been the most discussed character in History. What do we really know about Jesus today?

programs.title: The Quest for the Ark of the Covenant
programs.desc: In Judaism, it’s the most sacred object. A chest carved in acacia wood, gilded with gold leaf, and topped by two cherubs. The Ark of the Covenant strikes down the Mortal who touches it.

programs.title: The Quest for the Grail
programs.desc: It’s the most desired and sacred relic in Christianity. However, this artefact is shrouded in mystery. No one can say what it looks like. Today, dozens of churches claim to hold the Grail.

programs.title: The Power of King Solomon
programs.desc: Solomon is a mythical figure of the Old Testament. Third king of Israel, he reigned from 970 to 931 BC. But did he really exist?

programs.title: The Mystery of Fátima
programs.desc: The Shrine of Fatima in Portugal is one of the most visited pilgrimage sites in the world. More than 6 million visitors come every year to take a moment in this place.

programs.title: Camp Century
programs.desc: In 1959 the USA decided to build a military town under the ice sheet of North Greenland. The superpower wanted to use all its might to gain a strategic advantage over the Soviet Union.

programs.title: Life behind the Walls of Europe's Castles
programs.desc: What was life like behind a castle walls? The documentary follows their development from simple wooden fortifications to the most elaborate strongholds and residences.

programs.title: Enemy at the Gate
programs.desc: Castles were bastions of power. Yet, what if the enemy was at the gates? Our documentary examines the military function of castles from the 11th to the 16th century.

programs.title: Tinderbox Yugoslavia
programs.desc: Under the influence of changing rulers and empires, the country’s structure is formed over centuries as home to five nationalities with three languages and four different religions.

programs.title: A State Falls Apart
programs.desc: We are in the fateful year of Yugoslavia’s first free elections since World War II: 1990. It is the hour of the nationalists.

programs.title: Yugoslavia in Ruins
programs.desc: The Srebrenica massacre is a wake-up call for the international community, which decides to intervene after four years of war. That same year, the warring parties sign a peace treaty.

programs.title: The Balkans in Flames
programs.desc: The documentary THE BALKANS IN FLAMES examines the disintegration of the former Socialist Federation of Yugoslavia.

programs.title: The Seeds of Violence 1918-1922
programs.desc: Hatred and the desire for revenge smoldered in the minds of many Germans after the First World War. Many Germans believe that the Jews are the cause of all kinds of problems.

programs.title: Deceit and Delusion 1923-1928
programs.desc: Hitler and his movement seem to be eliminated after his failed putsch on November 9, 1923, the movement is banned, the self-proclaimed leaders are imprisoned.

programs.title: Democracy without Democrats 1929-1933
programs.desc: In the late 1920s, Germany was seething. Social protest turns into a racist and anti-Jewish movement, Hitler and his NSDAP using their anger against the “system” for their own benefits.

programs.title: The Racial State 1933-1934
programs.desc: After the 1933 parliament fire, President Hindenburg signs a decree that suspends freedom of speech. In mock elections, Hitler secures approval; with terror, he intimi-dates his adversaries.

programs.title: Hidden in Plain Sight 1935-1938
programs.desc: In October 1934, Hitler's government is firmly in the saddle. The majority of Germans support Hitler's offensive anti-Jewish policy.

programs.title: Up in Flames 1936-1940
programs.desc: At the end of 1939, the German Army has invaded Poland. They are followed closely by the SS (Schutzstaffel) task forces, which have only one mission: To murder the Polish intelligence.

programs.title: Auschwitz One Day
programs.desc: Harrowing testimonials from victims show how in 1944 the SS stepped up the “efficiency” of the death factory at Auschwitz and how the perpetrators documented their “work”.

programs.title: The Royals, the British Aristocracy and the Nazis
programs.desc: "The Royals, the British Aristocracy and the Nazis" presents documents and footage proving the royal family’s and leading British aristocrats’ sympathy for National Socialism.

programs.title: The Moon Landing and the Nazis
programs.desc: The film "The Moon Landing and the Nazis" documents the involvement of German NASA employees with the Third Reich.

programs.title: Concrete Against Bombs
programs.desc: The first programme features four bunkers built before World War Two. We begin with the legendary Franzensfeste in today’s northern Italy, a fortress that was never besieged.

programs.title: Facing Nuclear Annihilation
programs.desc: The second programme features shelters in the nuclear era in Lithuania, Germany and Albania.

programs.title: What if Hitler Had Won the War
programs.desc: The documentary addresses the counterfactual question of a Nazi victory in the Second World War and is asking at the same time how history would have evolved without Hitler.
